walkthroughs.body_html:
Forces & Motion — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Forces & Motion brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Forces & Motion.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 2 kg object accelerates at 4 m/s². What is the resultant force?
options: 2 N
8 N
6 N

mcqs.q: What does it mean if the resultant force on an object is zero?
options: The object must be stationary.
The object is either stationary or moving at constant velocity.
The object is decelerating.
The object is accelerating.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N) and depends on g.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Mass and weight are the same thing, just expressed in different units.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resultant force”?
options: The single force that has the same effect as all forces acting on an object combined.
A diagram showing all forces acting on a single object as arrows from its centre.
The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
Contact forces require touching (friction, tension); non-contact act at a distance (gravity, magnetism).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Force”?
options: The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
A push or pull that can change an object's shape, speed or direction. Measured in newtons (N).
Contact forces require touching (friction, tension); non-contact act at a distance (gravity, magnetism).
The single force that has the same effect as all forces acting on an object combined.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass”?
options: A push or pull that can change an object's shape, speed or direction. Measured in newtons (N).
The amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg). Does not change with location.
Contact forces require touching (friction, tension); non-contact act at a distance (gravity, magnetism).
The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Free-body diagram”?
options: The amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg). Does not change with location.
The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
Contact forces require touching (friction, tension); non-contact act at a distance (gravity, magnetism).
A diagram showing all forces acting on a single object as arrows from its centre.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Weight”?
options: Contact forces require touching (friction, tension); non-contact act at a distance (gravity, magnetism).
The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
A diagram showing all forces acting on a single object as arrows from its centre.
The single force that has the same effect as all forces acting on an object combined.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Contact vs non-contact”?
options: The single force that has the same effect as all forces acting on an object combined.
The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
Contact forces require touching (friction, tension); non-contact act at a distance (gravity, magnetism).
A push or pull that can change an object's shape, speed or direction. Measured in newtons (N).
